_meta.what: Opaque stubs for CodeMap's generated layer: the places where behaviour passes through a registry, hook or signal that a parser cannot follow. Each stub says where the parser goes blind, what explains it, and optionally how to list the real edges.
_meta.read_by: ~/Allie/scripts/wc-code-graph.py (build checks every anchor and every explained_by path; a missing one fails the build)
_meta.fields: id, kind, name, why_opaque, anchor, enters_from, reaches, covers (globs over file::function), kinds, explained_by[], resolver, owner, dt_reviewed

stubs.name: Save door behaviours
stubs.why_opaque: The door looks a model's behaviour up by model key at run time (behaviour_for) and calls before_<verb> / after_<verb> by name (ModelBehaviour.hook); no direct call exists in the code.

stubs.name: Commands (verbs on a model)
stubs.why_opaque: POST /wcapi/<model>/<id>/<command>/ finds its base service in the COMMANDS table, filled by register_command from each app's ready(); the caller is a URL.

stubs.name: Django signals
stubs.why_opaque: A handler runs when any code saves or deletes a row of its sender; the connection is made at import or in a register_* function, often with the sender passed in as a variable.
stubs.reaches: resolved (handlers); who fires them is unknown — any .save() or .delete() of the sender

stubs.name: Celery tasks and the beat schedule
stubs.why_opaque: A task runs when the beat schedule in settings.py names it or code calls .delay(); the name is a string and the run is in another process.
